indicators.statement: City ordinance/EO creating the CDRRMO as a regular office (not ad hoc), with defined functions mirroring RA 10121 Sec. 12(c)
CDRRMC constituted with complete membership per RA 10121 Sec. 11 (incl. CSO and private sector reps)
indicators.means_of_verification: EO on CDRRMC composition; list of members

indicators.statement: CDRRMC meets at least quarterly (and as needed); minutes and resolutions on file
CDRRMO serves as CDRRMC secretariat with documented secretariat procedures
Local DRRM-related ordinances in force (e.g., pre-emptive/forced evacuation, no-build zones, hazard-based zoning)
Protocol for declaring a State of Calamity, incl. CDRRMC recommendation steps and post-declaration measures (State of Imminent Disaster now assessed separately under A1.8)
DRRM is represented in City Development Council and Local Finance Committee deliberations

State of Imminent Disaster procedure: CDRRMC coordinates with RDRRMC VIII when the pre-disaster risk assessment shows reasonable certainty of severe impact; request format to RDRRMC (24-hour reply); Mayor's EO template; adoption rule when the Region (or Province, applicability to an ICC to be confirmed) is declared; lifting grounds and authority
indicators.reference: RA 12287; RA 12287 IRR (2026) Rule II Sec. 6; Rule III Secs. 2-4
indicators.means_of_verification: SOP; EO template; CDRRMC resolution and RDRRMC request templates

indicators.statement: Organizational structure follows JMC 2014-1: Head + Administration & Training, Research & Planning, and Operations & Warning divisions
CDRRMO Head is a permanent plantilla position filled by a qualified appointee
Minimum plantilla positions per JMC 2014-1 created and filled (ratio of filled/required)
Job descriptions/position descriptions defined for every position, aligned to RA 10121 functions
24/7 operations capability with documented shift roster (Operations Center/Duty officers)
Training needs analysis done and competency-based training plan for staff (ICS, BLS/SFA, WASAR, CSSR, MOSAR, EOC, PDNA, GIS)
indicators.reference: RA 10121 Sec. 14; OCD/DRRM Training Institute curricula

indicators.statement: Personnel welfare and safety: insurance, hazard pay, PPE, psychosocial support for responders
indicators.means_of_verification: Insurance policy; PPE inventory; MHPSS program

indicators.statement: Volunteer/auxiliary responder management system (accreditation, registry, deployment, insurance), incl. mobilization of ACDVs for anticipatory action
indicators.reference: RA 10121 Sec. 13; NDRRMC volunteer guidelines; RA 12287 IRR (2026) Rule IV Sec. 5

indicators.statement: Anticipatory action focal person designated in the CDRRMO, with AA training for staff, BDRRMCs, ACDVs and partner CSOs (incl. community-based early warning and early action)
indicators.reference: RA 12287 IRR (2026) Rule IV Sec. 1; Rule VII

indicators.statement: Inventory of DRRM-relevant skills across the CDRRMO, partner offices and barangays (SAR, engineering, logistics, GIS, PDNA, MHPSS) updated within the last 12 months
Local DRRM Plan (LDRRMP) current, approved by Sanggunian, aligned with NDRRMP 2020-2030 and Sendai Framework
DRR-CCA mainstreamed in CDP, CLUP, ELA and LCCAP (hazard data used in land use and investment decisions)
indicators.reference: RA 10121 Sec. 2; RA 9729 as amended by RA 10174; HLURB/DHSUD CLUP guidelines

indicators.statement: Hazard-specific Contingency Plans for priority hazards (flood/flash flood, landslide, earthquake/tsunami, tropical cyclone, industrial/geothermal), updated and tested
indicators.reference: NDRRMC CP guidelines; OCD CP Manual

indicators.statement: Public Service Continuity Plan (PSCP) prepared covering CDRRMO and essential city services
Annual LDRRMF Investment Plan (LDRRMFIP) prepared, approved and consistent with LDRRMP
Evacuation plan with mapped routes, safe zones, centers and pre-emptive evacuation triggers per barangay
Barangay DRRM plans (85 barangays) reviewed/consolidated by CDRRMO
indicators.reference: RA 10121 Sec. 12(c)(6); DILG MC on BDRRM

indicators.statement: LDRRMF set at not less than 5% of estimated revenue from regular sources
70% Mitigation/Preparedness and 30% Quick Response Fund (QRF) allocation observed
Unexpended LDRRMF transferred to Special Trust Fund and used within 5 years
LDRRMF utilization rate monitored and reported (target >= 80% of current-year 70% fund)
Emergency procurement procedures (negotiated procurement - emergency cases) documented and pre-arranged (framework agreements, pre-qualified suppliers)

Anticipatory action funding pathway: LDRRMFIP sets an AA line within the cap of 10% of the 70% LDRRMF; other sources mapped (Special Trust Fund balances, donations, ODA); Budget, Accounting and BAC procedures allow immediate disbursement and observe the 30%/70% tranche rule around the 3-day lead time
indicators.means_of_verification: LDRRMFIP AA line; Budget/Accounting guidance; disbursement and procurement SOP

indicators.statement: Risk transfer/financing instruments explored (indemnity insurance of public assets, PSF access, partnerships)
indicators.reference: NDRRMP; RA 10174 (People's Survival Fund); DOF-BTr NIP

indicators.statement: Clean COA findings on LDRRMF in last audit year (or findings addressed)
indicators.means_of_verification: COA Annual Audit Report; action plan

indicators.statement: QRF and LDRRMF adequacy tested against the most severe credible scenario (e.g., a Thelma-type flash flood or Yolanda-strength typhoon), with the shortfall and other fund sources identified
indicators.means_of_verification: Costed scenario; LDRRMFIP; Budget Office analysis

indicators.statement: Updated hazard maps for all priority hazards (MGB, PHIVOLCS, PAGASA, GeoRiskPH/HazardHunterPH) at barangay scale
Climate & Disaster Risk Assessment (CDRA)/ CRA completed with exposure (population, buildings, critical facilities) and vulnerability data
Disaggregated population database (sex, age, disability, IP, pregnant/lactating) for at-risk households

indicators.statement: DRRM information system/ database with disaster event history, damage and losses (incl. 1991 flood, 2013 Yolanda, 2017 earthquake records)
Data privacy compliance for beneficiary and affected-population data (DPO, consent, data sharing agreements)
GIS capability (software, trained staff, updated base maps) within Research & Planning
One maintained, shared source of risk and readiness information (hazard maps, plans, contacts, readiness summary) open to CDRRMC member offices, with a public summary posted

Critical facilities list (EOC, hospitals, evacuation centers, water, power, telecom, bridges, port) with dependencies mapped as potential failure chains and used to set protection and restoration priorities
indicators.reference: UNDRR DRSC 2.3.1; RA 12287 IRR (2026) Rule I Sec. 5(b),(d)

indicators.statement: Agreed update cycle: hazard data every 3 years or less; exposure, vulnerability and critical-facility data every 18 months or less
indicators.means_of_verification: Update procedure; version dates of datasets

indicators.statement: Hazard-specific EWS operational for flood (incl. Anilao/Malbasag river systems), rain-induced landslide, tsunami (Ormoc Bay) and tropical cyclone
indicators.means_of_verification: EWS inventory; functionality logs; maps of sensors/gauges

indicators.statement: Warning thresholds linked to specific actions (alert levels -> pre-emptive evacuation, class/work suspension, State of Imminent Disaster request) in written protocols, built to take up NDRRMC impact-based triggers once issued
indicators.reference: RA 10121; RA 12287; RA 12287 IRR (2026) Rule II Sec. 2; DILG Operation L!sto

indicators.statement: Last-mile dissemination channels tested to barangay/purok level (sirens, radio, SMS/ECBS, social media, barangay criers)
indicators.reference: RA 10639 (Free Mobile Disaster Alerts); NDRRMC EWS

indicators.statement: Warnings issued in local language (Cebuano/ Ormocanon) and accessible formats (sign language, visual alerts for PWD)
Designated public information officer and risk communication plan (incl. rumor/misinformation management)
IEC program on hazards and preparedness with annual reach targets

Templates and channels for public notice of a State of Imminent Disaster and of the anticipatory actions required, incl. sector-specific impact-based advisories and reach to geographically isolated barangays

Participation in quarterly Nationwide Simultaneous Earthquake Drill (NSED) and hazard-specific drills with evaluation

indicators.statement: Prepositioned relief stocks/food packs and non-food items with inventory and replenishment triggers

indicators.statement: Schools, hospitals and critical facilities included in preparedness planning and drills
Refresher cycle (at least annual) set for trained responders, EOC staff and BDRRMC members, with attendance tracked
BDRRMCs can account for residents of affected puroks within 12 hours of impact (welfare check), shown in a drill or a real event
indicators.means_of_verification: Drill or AAR record; barangay reports

indicators.statement: Incident Command System institutionalized: EO on ICS, trained IMT roster, pre-designated Incident Commanders
Organized and trained response teams: SAR (WASAR/CSSR/HAZMAT as relevant), EMS/ambulance, fire coordination with BFP

indicators.statement: Response equipment and vehicles inventoried, serviceable and maintained (preventive maintenance schedule)

indicators.statement: Pre-Disaster Risk Assessment (PDRA) conducted before forecast hazards, with anticipatory actions recorded
indicators.reference: NDRRMC PDRA protocol; RA 12287; RA 12287 IRR (2026) Rule II Sec. 5

indicators.statement: Management of the Dead and Missing (MDM) and Rapid Damage Assessment & Needs Analysis (RDANA) teams designated and trained

Anticipatory action protocols by hazard and lead time: office-order templates for prepositioning (relief, medical supplies, animal feed, water and power for evacuation centers), deployment of heavy equipment, transport and personnel, pre-emptive evacuation incl. livestock and pets, CCCM, and safeguarding of critical infrastructure; aligned with CPs, Oplan L!sto and evacuation plans

Recovery data (damage, losses, livelihood, housing) tracked to completion
Psychosocial and livelihood recovery services coordinated with CSWDO, CHO, PESO
Pre-disaster recovery framework: roles, PDNA activation, temporary shelter, debris management and recovery fund sources agreed before an event

Regular reporting to OCD Region VIII/RDRRMC and DILG (SitReps, LDRRMF reports, Operation L!sto)
Monitoring & evaluation framework for LDRRMP with indicators and annual review
Full Disclosure Policy: LDRRMF and utilization posted publicly
After-action reviews conducted after significant events and lessons integrated into plans

EOC established by EO/ordinance with defined mandate, authority and relationship to CDRRMC and ICS

indicators.statement: Activation, escalation, de-escalation and deactivation procedures with designated authority
Concept of operations documents EOC functions: coordination, information management, resource management, policy support
EOC linkage to Provincial (Leyte) and Regional (OCD VIII) EOCs defined
EOC site located outside high flood, landslide, tsunami and liquefaction zones (checked vs hazard maps)
Building structural integrity assessed (seismic - Philippine Fault proximity) and certified
Backup power (generator + fuel for >=72 hours, UPS) tested regularly
Functional layout: operations floor, briefing/decision room, comms room, rest area, sanitation, kitchen
Water, food and sanitation supplies for EOC staff for >=72 hours
Physical security and access control (ID, visitor log, CCTV)
Designated and equipped alternate EOC with relocation procedure
Redundant communications: VHF/UHF radio, HF, satellite phone, landline, mobile, internet (min. 3 independent channels)

indicators.statement: Radio network covering all 85 barangays and responders, with call signs and net-control procedure
Backup internet (secondary ISP/satellite) and continuity of digital systems
Communications plan/ directory (agencies, barangays, clusters) updated within last 6 months
Cybersecurity and information security measures for EOC systems
Display and monitoring equipment (video wall/monitors, weather feeds, CCTV feeds)
EOC organizational structure defined (EOC Manager, Operations, Planning/Information, Logistics, Admin/Finance, liaison desks)
Pre-designated EOC staff with alternates (at least 2 deep per key position)
Duty roster for sustained 24/7 operations with shift handover protocol
Agency/cluster liaison desks identified (CSWDO, CHO, CEO, PNP, BFP, AFP, DepEd, utilities, Red Cross)
Position checklists/job action sheets for each EOC role
Responder welfare in EOC: rest cycles, meals, MHPSS, family support
Standard SitRep/ Report templates aligned with NDRRMC/OCD formats and fixed reporting schedule
Barangay-to-city reporting flow (BDRRMC -> EOC) with defined timelines and formats
Common Operating Picture maintained (dashboard/ GIS map of incidents, evacuees, resources)
Evacuation center and affected-family tracking (DAFAC/ registration) feeds EOC data
EOC logbook/ significant events log and document retention
Weather/hazard monitoring routine (PAGASA, PHIVOLCS feeds) with bulletins logged and disseminated
Inbound citizen reporting (hotline, SMS, social media) feeds the common operating picture after a verification step
ICS-EOC interface defined: EOC supports Incident Commander(s); no duplication of command

indicators.statement: Resource management system: request, tracking, mobilization and demobilization of resources
Resource inventory (city, barangays, partners, private sector) accessible from EOC
Procedures for receiving and managing external assistance/ donations and volunteers
indicators.reference: NDRRMC guidelines on international/ external assistance

indicators.statement: Decision-support briefings to CDRRMC/Mayor at fixed intervals during activation
Pre-arranged resource commitments from partners and suppliers set out by item, quantity, activation trigger and contact in signed agreements (incl. supplier agreements tapped for anticipatory action)
indicators.reference: UNDRR DRSC 1.2.4; RA 12287 IRR (2026) Rule IV Sec. 6(a)(ii)

EOC staff trained (EOC operations course, ICS, IM) with records

Dedicated EOC budget for operations, maintenance and upgrades in LDRRMFIP
Equipment maintenance schedule and annual EOC readiness self-check

Risk-sensitive development guidelines applied in zoning and building permits, based on hazard maps
Structural safety of the EOC, evacuation centers and critical public facilities assessed by the Building Official, with a rapid safety inspection procedure before forecast impact
indicators.reference: UNDRR DRSC 4.3.1, 4.4.2; PD 1096; RA 12076; RA 12287 IRR (2026) Rule IV Sec. 4(c)(i)

Environmental anticipatory actions: declogging of waterways and drainage, slope stabilization, safe debris and carcass disposal

Education anticipatory action: schools' AA plans and learning-continuity modalities

# MOO Ch.1 – Legal and Institutional Framework

> Skeleton generated from IAT v1.1. Replace each requirement with the City's procedure, standard or form.

## Requirements this section must meet

- **A1.1** (M, weight 3) City ordinance/EO creating the CDRRMO as a regular office (not ad hoc), with defined functions mirroring RA 10121 Sec. 12(c)  
  *Basis:* RA 10121 Sec. 12; IRR Rule 6; JMC 2014-1
- **A1.2** (M, weight 2) CDRRMC constituted with complete membership per RA 10121 Sec. 11 (incl. CSO and private sector reps)  
  *Basis:* RA 10121 Sec. 11
- **A1.3** (M, weight 2) CDRRMC meets at least quarterly (and as needed); minutes and resolutions on file  
  *Basis:* RA 10121 Sec. 11; GKS/SGLG functionality criteria
- **A1.5** (GP, weight 2) Local DRRM-related ordinances in force (e.g., pre-emptive/forced evacuation, no-build zones, hazard-based zoning)  
  *Basis:* RA 10121 Sec. 12(c)(19); RA 7160; CLUP/ZO
- **A1.6** (M, weight 3) Protocol for declaring a State of Calamity, incl. CDRRMC recommendation steps and post-declaration measures (State of Imminent Disaster now assessed separately under A1.8)  
  *Basis:* RA 10121 Sec. 16
- **A1.7** (GP, weight 1) DRRM is represented in City Development Council and Local Finance Committee deliberations  
  *Basis:* RA 7160; JMC 2013-1
- **A1.8** (M, weight 3) State of Imminent Disaster procedure: CDRRMC coordinates with RDRRMC VIII when the pre-disaster risk assessment shows reasonable certainty of severe impact; request format to RDRRMC (24-hour reply); Mayor's EO template; adoption rule when the Region (or Province, applicability to an ICC to be confirmed) is declared; lifting grounds and authority  
  *Basis:* RA 12287; RA 12287 IRR (2026) Rule II Sec. 6; Rule III Secs. 2-4

  *Basis:* RA 10121 Sec. 12(c)(6); NDRRMP 2020-2030
- **A3.2** (M, weight 2) DRR-CCA mainstreamed in CDP, CLUP, ELA and LCCAP (hazard data used in land use and investment decisions)  
  *Basis:* RA 10121 Sec. 2; RA 9729 as amended by RA 10174; HLURB/DHSUD CLUP guidelines
- **A3.3** (M, weight 3) Hazard-specific Contingency Plans for priority hazards (flood/flash flood, landslide, earthquake/tsunami, tropical cyclone, industrial/geothermal), updated and tested  
  *Basis:* NDRRMC CP guidelines; OCD CP Manual
- **A3.4** (M, weight 2) Public Service Continuity Plan (PSCP) prepared covering CDRRMO and essential city services  
  *Basis:* NDRRMC/OCD PSCP Guidebook
- **A3.7** (GP, weight 2) Barangay DRRM plans (85 barangays) reviewed/consolidated by CDRRMO  
  *Basis:* RA 10121 Sec. 12(c)(6); DILG MC on BDRRM
- **A5.1** (M, weight 3) Updated hazard maps for all priority hazards (MGB, PHIVOLCS, PAGASA, GeoRiskPH/HazardHunterPH) at barangay scale  
  *Basis:* RA 10121 Sec. 12(c)(3); NDRRMP
- **A5.2** (M, weight 3) Climate & Disaster Risk Assessment (CDRA)/ CRA completed with exposure (population, buildings, critical facilities) and vulnerability data

- **A5.3** (M, weight 2) Disaggregated population database (sex, age, disability, IP, pregnant/lactating) for at-risk households

- **A5.8** (GP, weight 2) Critical facilities list (EOC, hospitals, evacuation centers, water, power, telecom, bridges, port) with dependencies mapped as potential failure chains and used to set protection and restoration priorities  
  *Basis:* UNDRR DRSC 2.3.1; RA 12287 IRR (2026) Rule I Sec. 5(b),(d)
- **A7.6** (M, weight 2) Inclusive DRRM: GAD, PWD, senior citizen, children, IP considerations embedded in plans and services, with vulnerable-sector representatives confirming they were engaged  
  *Basis:* RA 9710; RA 7277 as amended; RA 9994; RA 10821; RA 8371; RA 12287 IRR (2026) Rule IV Sec. 1(a); UNDRR DRSC 7.2.2
- **C1.1** (GP, weight 2) Most-probable and most-severe risk scenarios inform CDP/CLUP priorities and the location of major investments  
  *Basis:* UNDRR DRSC 1.1.1; RA 10121 Sec. 2; DHSUD CLUP guidelines
- **C1.2** (GP, weight 1) DRR/CCA screening step in project and budget approval (LDC, LFC)

  *Basis:* UNDRR DRSC 2.2.2; DHSUD/CCC CDRA guidelines
- **C1.4** (GP, weight 2) Risk-sensitive development guidelines applied in zoning and building permits, based on hazard maps  
  *Basis:* UNDRR DRSC 2.4.1; CLUP/ZO
- **C3.1** (GP, weight 2) Critical protective ecosystems (upper Anilao-Malbasag watershed, upland forest cover, coastal mangroves) identified and monitored as risk-reduction assets  
  *Basis:* UNDRR DRSC 5.1.1; RA 9729 as amended

  *Basis:* JMC 2013-1
- **A4.1** (M, weight 3) LDRRMF set at not less than 5% of estimated revenue from regular sources  
  *Basis:* RA 10121 Sec. 21; JMC 2013-1
- **A4.2** (M, weight 3) 70% Mitigation/Preparedness and 30% Quick Response Fund (QRF) allocation observed  
  *Basis:* RA 10121 Sec. 21; JMC 2013-1
- **A4.3** (M, weight 2) Unexpended LDRRMF transferred to Special Trust Fund and used within 5 years  
  *Basis:* RA 10121 Sec. 21; COA Circular 2012-002
- **A4.4** (GP, weight 2) LDRRMF utilization rate monitored and reported (target >= 80% of current-year 70% fund)  
  *Basis:* JMC 2013-1; COA AAR findings
- **A4.5** (M, weight 2) Emergency procurement procedures (negotiated procurement - emergency cases) documented and pre-arranged (framework agreements, pre-qualified suppliers)  
  *Basis:* RA 12009 (New Government Procurement Act) & IRR
- **A4.6** (M, weight 2) Anticipatory action funding pathway: LDRRMFIP sets an AA line within the cap of 10% of the 70% LDRRMF; other sources mapped (Special Trust Fund balances, donations, ODA); Budget, Accounting and BAC procedures allow immediate disbursement and observe the 30%/70% tranche rule around the 3-day lead time  
  *Basis:* RA 12287; RA 12287 IRR (2026) Rule V Secs. 1-3; RA 10121 Sec. 21; RA 12009

protocol_templates.title: Duty shift handover
protocol_templates.trigger_text: Every change of duty shift at the Operations Center.

protocol_templates.title: Warning dissemination
protocol_templates.purpose: Move a hazard bulletin to every at-risk purok, in a form people understand.
protocol_templates.trigger_text: On receipt of a PAGASA, PHIVOLCS or MGB bulletin or advisory that affects Ormoc.

protocol_templates.title: EOC activation (Blue or Red)
protocol_templates.purpose: Stand up the EOC quickly with the right people and records.
protocol_templates.trigger_text: When the EOC Manager raises the level to Blue or Red.

protocol_templates.title: Pre-disaster risk assessment (PDRA)
protocol_templates.purpose: Decide, from the forecast and local exposure, whether to monitor, act early or request a declaration.
protocol_templates.trigger_text: When a forecast hazard may affect Ormoc.

protocol_templates.title: State of Imminent Disaster: request and declaration
protocol_templates.purpose: Follow RA 12287 and its IRR from the PDRA to the Mayor's Executive Order.
protocol_templates.trigger_text: When the PDRA shows severe impact with at least 3 days of lead time.

protocol_templates.title: Flash flood and landslide early action
protocol_templates.purpose: Act on short-lead hazards that cannot wait for a declaration.
protocol_templates.trigger_text: When rainfall or river readings reach the City's early-action thresholds for the Anilao–Malbasag system or upland barangays.

protocol_templates.title: SitRep cycle
protocol_templates.purpose: Produce a verified SitRep on schedule every operational period.
protocol_templates.trigger_text: At each scheduled SitRep time during an activation.

protocol_templates.title: CDRRMC meeting (secretariat)
protocol_templates.purpose: Run the Council meeting and keep its records complete.
protocol_templates.trigger_text: Quarterly, and whenever the Chair calls a special meeting.

protocol_templates.title: Lifting and 45-day report
protocol_templates.purpose: Lift a State of Imminent Disaster correctly and report to OCD on time.
protocol_templates.trigger_text: When the hazard occurs or the PDRA shows the projected impacts will not be met.

protocol_steps.instruction: Read the logbook entries since the last handover
Review open incidents, resource requests and pending barangay reports
Check the latest PAGASA and PHIVOLCS bulletins and record any change
Run the radio net check with the barangays scheduled for this shift
Check generator fuel, UPS and backup internet status
Record handover notes and sign off with the incoming duty officer
Log the bulletin: issuer, number, time issued, hazard and areas
Check it against the City warning-to-action matrix and note the matching alert and actions
Notify the EOC Manager and CDRRMO Head; record the instruction received
Issue the advisory in Cebuano, with Filipino/English and accessible formats as needed
Send through every channel: emergency cell broadcast/SMS, radio, social media, barangay officials
Confirm receipt from riverine, coastal and upland barangays first, then the rest
Log barangays that did not confirm and assign follow-up
Record the level change and reason in the platform (logs it automatically). If no device can connect, write it in the paper logbook with the time and enter it once connected
Notify CDRRMC members, cluster leads and liaison desks of the activation
Fill EOC positions from the roster, with alternates
Run the communications check on all redundant channels
Set the operational period and the SitRep schedule
Brief the Mayor on the situation and decisions needed
Convene the PDRA core group and record attendance by office
Review the forecast: hazard, expected impact time, areas, impact level
Identify exposed barangays, vulnerable groups, critical facilities and possible cascading hazards
Classify the projected impact and compute the lead time left
Decide: monitor, city early action, or request a State of Imminent Disaster; record the basis
Record the PDRA in the platform and brief the CDRRMO Head
Prepare the CDRRMC request to RDRRMC VIII with the PDRA results
Send the request and record the time sent (RDRRMC replies within 24 hours)
Record the RDRRMC recommendation and its reference
Prepare the Mayor's Executive Order for signature
Record the EO number and time of declaration
Issue official public notice of the declaration and the actions required
Load the anticipatory action checklist and assign lead offices
Record the reading, gauge or source, and the threshold reached
Alert riverine and upland BDRRMCs by radio and SMS
Recommend pre-emptive evacuation of the identified puroks to the EOC Manager
Open the designated evacuation centres and alert CSWDO
Position rescue teams at the agreed staging points
Confirm evacuation counts from each barangay and log them
Collect barangay reports and cluster updates since the last SitRep
Reconcile evacuation figures with evacuation-centre counts
Draft the SitRep in the standard format
EOC Manager reviews and approves
Submit to OCD VIII and the Province; record the time sent
